solutions.check: clues read from the FT's printable PDF (PDF has no vector grid), the grid backsolved from their numbering, the one grid that fits; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A comedian's funny country

indicators.note: funny suggests something odd or peculiar, so the letters of these words get rearranged

parts.note: the words taken as written, the possessive 's giving no letter

explanation.surface: A stand-up comic's routine is set in some amusing nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges the letters of A COMEDIAN; the 's adds nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedonia is a nation in the Balkans, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Woman married man

parts.note: Abel, son of Adam and Eve, is a crossword's stock man

explanation.surface: A woman wed a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Mabel is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Wrapper to hang on picture

parts.note: to cling is to hang on tightly
a picture, in the sense of a movie, is a film

explanation.surface: Wrapping paper to hang on to a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Cling film is thin plastic sheeting used to wrap food.

clue.text: Queen with youth leader in rude revue? I am surprised!

indicators.note: the youth leader goes inside the queen

parts.note: Dido was the legendary queen of Carthage

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter, here of youth
rude here means rough or crude, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A monarch and a youth leader appear in an indecent stage show, to everyone's astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Dido was the legendary queen of Carthage. 'in' puts the leader of youth inside her, and 'rude' scrambles the show's name into UEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Did you ever! is an exclamation of astonishment.

clue.text: Chairman's back with directors in passage

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, here of chairman

parts.note: arrows are signs that direct the way

explanation.surface: The chair is back, along with the board, in the corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'directors' suggests a board of company directors; it means things that point the way, ARROWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrows is a narrow stretch of water, a strait or channel passage between two larger bodies.

clue.text: Song about swine in pastoral setting

indicators.note: about means around, so the song is placed around the swine

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
a swine is a contemptible man, a cad

explanation.surface: A ballad about pigs set in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swine' suggests pigs on a farm; it means a rotter, a CAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is the idealised rustic paradise of poetry, a byword for an idyllic countryside.

clue.text: Sue needs introduction to punk and heavy metal

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter, here of punk

parts.note: lead is a famously heavy metallic element

explanation.surface: Someone called Sue needs a primer on punk rock and heavy metal music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' looks like a woman's name but is the verb, to take to court; 'heavy metal' looks like the music genre but is the element LEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue is to make a case in court, and to plead is likewise to argue a case before a judge.

clue.text: Fresh supper-time sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the answer is held within the words

explanation.surface: Fresh food prepared at suppertime: sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like the food; it is the verb, holding letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh can mean cheeky or impudent, and pert is a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Turn out to see a tennis player

definitions.meaning: to turn inside out, especially an eyelid
Chris ..., the American champion of the 1970s and 1980s

explanation.surface: Show up to watch a tennis star.
explanation.definitionFit: To evert is to turn something outward, and Chris Evert was a leading American tennis champion.

clue.text: Small charge observed when climbing a hill

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means going upward, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: observed means noted
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A small explosive charge observed while hikers scale a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses NOTED to give DETON; a tor is a rocky hilltop in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonator is the small explosive device that sets off a larger charge.

clue.text: Screen closed at one end

definitions.meaning: a window screen, a roller shade pulled down to block light
as in a ... alley, a street with no way through at its far end

explanation.surface: A screen that has been shut at one of its edges.
explanation.definitionFit: A window shade is a blind, and a dead-end alley is called a blind alley because it has no exit.

clue.text: Extremely rare flower — perennial?

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here of rare

parts.note: read as flow-er, something that flows, such as a current of water

explanation.surface: An unusual bloom that may come back each year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is not a bloom but a thing that flows, a crossword favourite for a river or CURRENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perennial keeps coming back, which is what a recurrent thing does by repeating itself.

clue.text: Car with sporty body in painting

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other, the sporty body placed inside the car

parts.note: Lagonda is a British luxury car marque
the IOC is the International Olympic Committee, which governs Olympic sport

explanation.surface: A car with an athletic-looking body shell shown in a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporty body' suggests a sleek car body; it is the Olympic governing committee, placed by 'in' inside a British luxury marque.
explanation.definitionFit: La Gioconda is the Italian title of Leonardo's portrait better known as the Mona Lisa.

clue.text: Crackpots turning bowl over

indicators.note: turning a word round means reading its letters from the end back to the start

parts.note: crackpots are eccentric people, informally nuts

explanation.surface: Eccentrics who flip a basin upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowl someone over is to astonish or overwhelm them, the same as to stun them.

clue.text: Man of principle hides cream crackers

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Dairy cream concealed among the biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like biscuits; it is the slang adjective for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes formulated the Archimedes principle of buoyancy, so he is literally a man known for a principle.

clue.text: Cricketers with one replacing wickets for old birds

indicators.note: the letter for one takes the place of the letter for wickets inside the cricketers word

parts.note: bowlers are cricketers who deliver the ball
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wickets
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Cricket players, swapping one item for another, turn into elderly birds.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler delivers the ball to the batter, and W stands for wickets; swapping it for I (one) gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiler is an older hen, tough enough only for stewing, so boilers are aged birds.

clue.text: Swedes, for example, taking money one almost threw away

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to cast something is to throw it away

explanation.surface: Scandinavians take some cash that one nearly discarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swedes' looks like people from Sweden; a swede is a root vegetable, called rutabaga in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Swedes belong to the cabbage family, the genus whose members are called brassicas.

clue.text: Fruit with cereal, mostly, in a container

indicators.note: the shortened cereal goes inside the container

parts.note: a pot is a container for cooking or storage

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: Fruit served with breakfast cereal, mostly kept in a tub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the grain's final letter, giving RIC, and 'in' sets that inside the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Recall what?

definitions.meaning: to come back again, a return or reprise
a request for someone to repeat what they said

explanation.surface: Asking someone to repeat what they just said.
explanation.definitionFit: Come again means return, a recall, and as a question it asks a speaker to repeat themselves.

clue.text: Support male kept in check

indicators.note: one piece is held inside the other, the male inside the check

parts.note: to check something is to halt it, to arrest it

explanation.surface: A man held under control for his own good.
explanation.definitionFit: An armrest is the part of a chair that props up your elbow, a kind of support.

clue.text: Royalist at sea drops old piece of canvas

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the remaining letters are jumbled
drops means loses, so the letter for old is taken away

explanation.surface: A Cavalier sailor lets slip a scrap of old sailcloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops old' removes O from ROYALIST, and 'at sea' rearranges RYALIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A trysail is a small strong sail, a sheet of canvas set in heavy weather.

clue.text: Machiavelli wanting a corrupt marchese

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or distorted, so the remaining letters are rearranged
wanting means lacking, so the letter a is removed from the Italian noble's title

explanation.surface: Machiavelli lacking a crooked Italian nobleman to advise.
explanation.walkthrough: A marchese is an Italian marquis; 'wanting a' removes one A and 'corrupt' rearranges the remaining MRCHESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Machiavelli, the Florentine political writer, gave his name to cunning plotting, so any devious plotter can be called one.

clue.text: King not attended by second knight

parts.note: solo means alone, unaccompanied
a mo is a moment, a second
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A monarch is unescorted, apart from a second knight.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is British slang for a moment, as in 'half a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Solomon was the son of David and king of Israel, famed for wisdom.

clue.text: Observe sound location

indicators.note: sound tells us the word is identified by how it is spoken

parts.note: to sight something is to observe it

explanation.surface: Watch out for a solid place to stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective, as in a sound location; it is the signal that SIGHT is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a place or position where something stands, a location.

clue.text: Put back sword in tent

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, here of put

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: Return the sword to the tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back' looks like an instruction to replace something or a reversal; it means the back letter of 'Put'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tepee is a conical tent used by Plains Indians of North America.

clue.text: Of course Ballymena's off course

indicators.note: off course means having strayed from the right path, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: Ballymena is a town in Northern Ireland, with its possessive s used

explanation.surface: Naturally, a Northern Irish town has strayed off the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Ballymena is a town in County Antrim, Northern Ireland; here the 's is used as an S. The clue plays 'Of course' against 'off course'.
explanation.definitionFit: By all means is an emphatic yes, the same assent as saying of course.

clue.text: Georgia or Virginia, say

parts.note: two American examples standing for a whole class; Georgia could also be the country in the Caucasus

explanation.definitionFit: Georgia and Virginia are both members of the US federation, each a constituent of the union.

clue.text: Composer is arranger, oddly enough

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd positions, first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: A musical writer turns out to be an arranger, surprisingly.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Arne was an 18th-century English composer, best known for 'Rule, Britannia!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arne, an 18th-century Englishman, wrote music for the stage.

clue.text: Biblical location to fix car up? Amen!

indicators.note: to fix something is to repair or rework it, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prayer to repair a broken-down car at a holy site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks like a reversal signal for car, but car, up and amen are all rearranged together under 'fix'.
explanation.definitionFit: Capernaum was a fishing town on the Sea of Galilee where the Gospels place much of Jesus' ministry.

clue.text: Drink associated with a theatrical production

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of whisky

explanation.surface: A drink linked to a stage show, as at an interval bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play, the kind of production staged in a theatre.

clue.text: Observed sound location

indicators.note: sound tells us the word is identified by how it is spoken

parts.note: observed means seen

explanation.surface: Spotted a solid place to be.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene is the place where something happens, as in the scene of the crime.

clue.text: Hanker, as in the distant past

parts.note: to hanker is to yearn or long
as and since both mean because

explanation.surface: Pining, as one did in days gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: Long since means a great while ago, far back in time.
